To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we show how to find all answers to a query in a system of heterogeneous sources by a simple translation of query and source descriptions into a Datalog program.

we can find the complete set of answers to a query with limited source capabilities by evaluating a simple program on the source data, and that the program can be optimized by removing useless off-query accesses.

(i) we can find all the answer to a query by using a simple recursive Dolog program that accesses all the source relations, even those that are not mentioned in the query; (ii) we can eliminate the unnecessary source accesses from this program; and (iii) we can find the useful source relations to answer the query.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems: (i) Given a source description and a query, find all the answers to the query by evaluating a simple program on the source data.
finding all the useful answers to a query with limited source capabilities, and optimizing query evaluation to eliminate unnecessary accesses.
the following issues. (1) How to translate queries and sources to Datalog. (2) How to find all the answers to a query.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is a complete solution to query optimization in the presence of limited sources, and is the first such solution.
we have developed a complete theory of query planning with limited sources.
our algorithm can find all answers to any query with sources that have limited query capabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a query planning algorithm for information-integration systems that uses sources not mentioned in the query, and eliminates the unnecessary accesses to these sources.
we show how to answer a query with limited sources, and optimize the query answering process by eliminating the unnecessary accesses.
we show that the sources not mentioned in the query can contribute to its answer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the query planning problem is more challenging in information-integration systems than in traditional database systems, because the system has limited access to information sources, and because some sources are useful for answering a query even though they are not in the original query.
sources not mentioned in the query can contribute to its answer.
we can find the answer to a query without having to query the source explicitly, by translating the query into a program that can be executed over the sources.
